neighbours.label: a first-person narrative action verb right after 'I' in a past-tense story (I asked, I went, I told)
fire: The driver stopped at the gate, and when he came back I asked him what had happened.
She looked worried at dinner, so later that night I asked her about the letter.
The shop was closed when we arrived, so I asked the guard when it would open.
He refused to answer at first, but the next morning I asked him again.
The road was blocked by snow, so I went back to the village and waited.
The old woman smiled at me, and I asked her how long she had lived there.
My brother was silent the whole trip, until finally I asked him what was wrong.
The teacher handed back the essays, and afterwards I asked her about my grade.
quiet: The driver stopped at the gate, and the barrier was raised a few minutes later.
She looked worried at dinner, and the letter lay unopened on the table all night.
The shop was closed when we arrived, and the windows were dark and dusty.
He refused to answer at first, and the room stayed quiet for a long while.
The road was blocked by snow, and the village was cut off for two days.
The old woman smiled at the children, and her house was warm and full of books.
My brother was silent the whole trip, and the car radio played old songs.
The teacher handed back the essays, and the class was noisy for the rest of the hour.

notes: Weak pole (max 12.6). Probe: only 'I asked him' scored (0.25); 'swore' 0.09; third-person action verbs ('went', 'said nothing') <=0.03; descriptive sentences <=0.05. The label is narrowed to first-person 'I asked'-type verbs (one fire item uses 'I went'). The median-fire bar is at risk.
